+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"log"
+	"net/http"
+	"regexp"
+	"sync"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/notes/notes/internal/store"
+)
+
+// credentialsMaxBytes is the largest request body signup and login read: a
+// username of 20 characters and a password of 1000, with room to spare.
+const credentialsMaxBytes = 4096
+
+// minPasswordLen is the shortest password the app accepts.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// validUsername is the account name the spec allows: lower-case letters,
+// digits and the underscore, three to twenty of them, nothing around them.
+var validUsername = regexp.MustCompile(`\A[a-z0-9_]{3,20}\z`)
+
+// registerAuth puts the account routes on the mux. GET /api/me belongs to
+// the auth card, so it replaces the foundation's placeholder here.
+func (s *server) registerAuth(mux *http.ServeMux) {
+	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/signup", s.signup)
+	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/login", s.login)
+	mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/logout", s.logout)
+	mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/me", s.me)
+}
+
+// credentials is what signup and login take: a name and a secret.
+type credentials struct {
+	Username string `json:"username"`
+	Password string `json:"password"`
+}
+
+// readCredentials decodes one request body into credentials. It answers ok
+// false once the response is already spoken for: bad JSON, an empty field or
+// a name or secret the rules refuse.
+func readCredentials(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (credentials, bool) {
+	var c credentials
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, credentialsMaxBytes)).Decode(&c); err != nil {
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusBadRequest, map[string]string{"error": "invalid JSON"})
+		return c, false
+	}
+	if !validUsername.MatchString(c.Username) {
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusBadRequest, map[string]string{"error": "username must be 3 to 20 characters of a-z, 0-9 and _"})
+		return c, false
+	}
+	if len(c.Password) < minPasswordLen {
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusBadRequest, map[string]string{"error": fmt.Sprintf("password must be at least %d characters", minPasswordLen)})
+		return c, false
+	}
+	return c, true
+}
+
+// startSession gives a signed-up or logged-in user its cookie: a fresh token
+// kept in the store, then written to the response.
+func (s *server) startSession(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, userID int64) error {
+	token, expires, err := NewSession()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	if _, err := s.store.CreateSession(userID, token, expires); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	SetSessionCookie(w, r, token, expires)
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (s *server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	c, ok := readCredentials(w, r)
+	if !ok {
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(c.Password), bcrypt.DefaultCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		log.Printf("signup: hash: %v", err)
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, map[string]string{"error": "try again"})
+		return
+	}
+	user, err := s.store.CreateUser(c.Username, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		// The name is unique in the store; anything else is a real failure.
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{"error": "that username is taken"})
+		return
+	}
+	if err := s.startSession(w, r, user.ID); err != nil {
+		log.Printf("signup: session for %d: %v", user.ID, err)
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, map[string]string{"error": "try again"})
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, userJSON(user))
+}
+
+func (s *server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	c, ok := readCredentials(w, r)
+	if !ok {
+		return
+	}
+	user, err := s.store.GetUserByUsername(c.Username)
+	if errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+		// Compare against a hash of its own, so an unknown name costs the
+		// same as a wrong password and answers the same words.
+		_ = bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword(unknownUserHash(), []byte(c.Password))
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "invalid username or password"})
+		return
+	}
+	if err != nil {
+		log.Printf("login: %v", err)
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, map[string]string{"error": "try again"})
+		return
+	}
+	if err := bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(user.PasswordHash), []byte(c.Password)); err != nil {
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "invalid username or password"})
+		return
+	}
+	if err := s.startSession(w, r, user.ID); err != nil {
+		log.Printf("login: session for %d: %v", user.ID, err)
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, map[string]string{"error": "try again"})
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, userJSON(user))
+}
+
+func (s *server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(c.Value); err != nil {
+			log.Printf("logout: %v", err)
+			writeJSON(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, map[string]string{"error": "try again"})
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	ClearSessionCookie(w, r)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+func (s *server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	userID, ok := currentUser(s.store, r)
+	if !ok {
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "unauthorized"})
+		return
+	}
+	// The session names a user id; the row behind it gives the username. A
+	// session whose user is gone is no login at all, so 401 as well.
+	user, err := s.store.GetUserByID(userID)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			log.Printf("me: %v", err)
+		}
+		writeJSON(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "unauthorized"})
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, userJSON(user))
+}
+
+// userJSON is the account as the API answers it: never the hash.
+func userJSON(u *store.User) map[string]any {
+	return map[string]any{
+		"id":         u.ID,
+		"username":   u.Username,
+		"created_at": u.CreatedAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
+	}
+}
+
+// unknownUserHash is the hash a login for a name nobody owns is compared
+// against: made once, of a password no signup can have offered.
+var unknownUserHash = sync.OnceValue(func() []byte {
+	h, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte("0123456789"), bcrypt.MinCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		// A hash bcrypt refuses to compare against: the mismatch is instant,
+		// and the answer the caller writes is the same 401 either way.
+		return []byte("!")
+	}
+	return h
+})
